messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — Lumos (enterprise fintech) is asking for a Dedicated GPU pool in asia-south1 for a POC. They expect steady 120 req/s (chat), avg ~80 tokens out, but can spike to ~400 req/s for short windows. They need low tail latency (aiming for 95th <= 250ms) and PCI compliance. Questions: 1) sku/size recommendation, 2) burst/autoscaling strategy, 3) provisioning lead time, 4) can we do an initial POC with hosted API keys before Dedicated?

kevin_solutions_eng: thanks — quick clarifying q: which model family do they plan to serve (7B, 13B, 70B)? latency/per-GPU throughput changes a lot. also are synchronous responses required (no streaming)?

maria_sales: calling out: they want to run a 13B class open model (LLM-13B-std) for now, synchronous streaming OK but prefer single-call latency.

alex_infra: for a 13B baseline: rough rule-of-thumb: 13B ~ 20-30 tokens/sec per A100-like GPU at typical configs. For steady 120 req/s * 80 tokens ~= 9.6k tokens/sec aggregate. Accounting for concurrency overhead and batching inefficiencies, I'd size ~6 GPUs of A100-class for steady, with autoscale headroom to handle bursts to 400 req/s (target ~10 GPUs). H100 would reduce GPU count (4 H100-ish) but adds lead-time and cost. Also recommend prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching to keep 95p latency down.

jordyn_sre: note on compliance & networking: for PCI we need Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with explicit network isolation + KMS integration. VPC peering + private endpoints + restricted egress. CIDR and security group config will be provided once we kick off the request. Also we need an ICO/security questionnaire answered — flagging that to sales.

kevin_solutions_eng: here's a small perf calc i pasted for the POC:
```
# approximate tokens/s needed
steady_tokens_per_sec = 120 * 80  # 9600
burst_tokens_per_sec = 400 * 80   # 32000
# effective tokens/sec per GPU (13B) ~ 25000 on H100, ~16000 on A100 (with batching)
# => steady: 9600/16000 = 0.6 GPUs  (A100)  => but overhead + concurrency => 6 GPUs recommended
# => burst: 32000/16000 = 2 GPUs (A100) => again increase for headroom -> autoscale to ~10 GPUs to keep tail low
```
kevin_solutions_eng: TL;DR recommendation: start with 6x A100-class dedicated nodes, autoscale policy to add up to 10 for 5-10 minute bursts, or 4x H100-class with autoscale to 6 (H100 option if they accept higher cost/lead-time). Enable KV prefix caching and aggressive batching (max latency target 50ms batch time).

sam_sales: rough budget question from Lumos — can you give a ballpark monthly committed vs on-demand price for 6 A100 vs 4 H100 for POC (they want a 30-day POC with possible expansion)?

alex_infra: roughs: 6 A100 reserved-ish for POC -> estimate $XXk/mo (I'll convert to concrete quote), 4 H100 -> ~1.6x that. exact depends on region/commit. Also note: provisioning ETA for A100 in asia-south1 is ~5 business days; H100 provisioning could be 10-15 business days depending on capacity.

deploy-bot: Pool request created: request_id=PR-2026-7843, sku_hint=A100-80GB, region=asia-south1, requested_by=maria_sales. Status: queued.

maria_sales: Can we do a hybrid approach — start POC on Hosted (with model runtime tuned) while dedicated pool is being provisioned? Lumos is ok with demo data initially but will need PCI-only for the full POC.

kevin_solutions_eng: yes — we can run an initial POC against Hosted API using dedicated model config and simulated load to validate latency and prompts. That will give a short feedback loop while the Dedicated pool is provisioning for the PCI-limited phase.

jordyn_sre: confirm: once Dedicated is ready we'll migrate traffic via routing policy and rotate keys. We'll need their KMS info + AOC for PCI scope. Schedule a short security sync with Lumos before cutover.

sam_sales: I'll ask for budget approval and ask Lumos if they prefer H100 option. maria, can you capture: required SLO (95p 250ms), POC length 30d, region asia-south1, model 13B, burst to 400 req/s, PCI required for full POC.

maria_sales: noted, will push that to Lumos and request answer on H100 preference. thanks all :thumbsup:
